title: Jelly's handwritten music and how he worked
summary: Jelly's manuscripts were neat; she did not see him write in Chicago but music was stacked at the piano.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I just wondered, because I have some arrangements that I got from this man—a man, a friend of mine who died in Washington, who had known your brother very well there, and had published some of his music. And when he died, he had some of his music there that he'd written out. It was supposed to be that—Jolly Roll wrote that out on the— Oh, yes. I mean, in his last days, he would write music. He wrote the rock, really beautiful.
That's right. Beautiful, very neat, wonderful.

And my son writes music beautifully, too. My son saxophonically. He writes music. He wrote—he wrote out a little song for—a little number for my grandson the other day to play on the piano. It really sounds good.

I just wondered if your brother had music around the piano, if he was writing it out in Chicago in those days. Well, not when he was sick when I was there. He didn't know. Not that you saw him do that?

No. I didn't see him do anything. Mm-hmm. When the bands was—when I would go down to see him after the bands had left, and I'd come to see him while the music would be stacked on the piano, you know what I mean? He wouldn't have music stacked on the piano.
Yes, uh-huh. So he could evidently read it very well then, that's how he learned to read it and could write it. That's right, that's right.
